title: Winter fuel payments for pension credit recipients only
headline: Pension credit recipients only. Saves £1.3bn in 2029-30.
description: From winter 2025 winter fuel payments in England and Wales go to pensioners with taxable income of £35,000 or less, with the payment recovered through the tax system from higher-income pensioners. Switch this on to return to paying only pension credit recipients from winter 2027, saving the Treasury's costing of the wider payment (£1.3bn in 2029-30).

baselinePolicy.text: Winter fuel payments targeted at pensioners with taxable income at or below £35,000 from winter 2025, at a cost of £1.8bn in 2025-26 and about £1.3bn a year by 2029-30 (Budget 2025, Table 4.1 line 84).
alreadyIncludes: Winter fuel payments for pensioners with taxable income of £35,000 or less from winter 2025 (Budget 2025, Table 4.1 line 84).

lines.title: Winter Fuel Payment: Target to pensioners with taxable income below or equal to £35,000 from Winter 2025

rawSource.note: Reversal on the spending side: the Treasury's costing with the sign kept (a measure that increased borrowing was more spending; reversing it is the same amount of spending saved).

caveats: The Treasury's costing is on the OBR November 2025 forecast, not the March 2026 baseline used here; the difference is small relative to the figures. Effects before the start year are not applied.

considerations.text: Winter heating assistance is devolved in Scotland and winter fuel payments are a transferred matter in Northern Ireland. The Treasury presents the costing on a UK-wide basis, including the resulting changes to the Scottish block grant adjustment and Northern Ireland Executive funding; the devolved governments decide their own schemes.
The Treasury's costing allows for more pensioners opting out of the payment where it would be recovered by HMRC, and names the size of that response as its main uncertainty.

The Treasury's scorecard figure is the certified direct costing for the measure, including the behavioural response the Treasury and OBR agreed; see the Budget 2025 policy costings document for the method.
